title: Integrated Fuzzy Logic Model for Assessing and Selecting Services in the Internet of Things Ecosystem Based on Quality of Service
content: Recent years have witnessed a significant increase in the number of Internet of Things (IoT) connected devices, producing many functionally similar services that differ in non-functional attributes such as Quality of Service (QoS). Evaluating QoS reliably is complicated by IoTʹs multilayer architecture and inherent uncertainty in consumer preferences, and selecting services on preference alone risks overqualification and inefficient resource use. This study proposes an integrated assessment and selection model. First, a two-stage fuzzy logic method evaluates the QoS of registered IoT services across all architectural layers. Second, candidate services are filtered according to both user preference and task purpose, then ranked using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Experiments on a 200-service dataset showed that the assessment model successfully estimated QoS for every service. In a critical-purpose scenario, the model automatically selected 67 high-quality candidate services; in a normal-purpose, low-QoS scenario, it identified 21 low-quality services. The two-stage approach also reduced service-ranking execution time relative to an AHP-TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) baseline. By incorporating task purpose alongside user preference, the proposed model mitigates service overqualification, improves ranking efficiency, and gives IoT service providers a practical tool for matching services to end-user requirements.
